clue.text: Team calls party organised "fantastic!"

indicators.note: something organised has been arranged afresh, so the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
ace is slang for excellent or fantastic

explanation.surface: A sports team declares that the party it has organised is fantastic.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation 'fantastic!' looks like a quotation but supplies its own letters to the mix. Crystal Palace is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Crystal Palace is the name of an English football club, so it is an example of a team.

clue.text: Join one canal somewhere north of New York

blocks.note: to join is to connect
Roman numeral one
a cut is a man-made waterway, an old word for a canal

explanation.surface: Directions to link up with a canal somewhere in the north-eastern United States.
explanation.walkthrough: CUT for a canal is a British usage, from the cutting dug to make it.
explanation.definitionFit: Connecticut is a US state lying north-east of New York City and bordering New York State, so it is a vague location clue.

clue.text: One-time conference venue set up by volunteers

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: to set something down is to lay it
the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A historic meeting place that was arranged by volunteer helpers.
explanation.definitionFit: Yalta in Crimea hosted the 1945 summit of Churchill, Roosevelt and Stalin, a famous wartime conference location.

clue.text: Fair charge ultimately included in cost for part-time staff?

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the preceding word
being included in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: the rate of pay for a temp, a temporary worker
final letter of charge

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a reasonable fee is built into the budget for temporary workers.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the cost phrase is a made-up description rather than a fixed term.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair weather is mild weather, and temperate describes a mild climate, a synonym in that sense.

clue.text: Lively ethos embraced by large old country

indicators.note: lively suggests energetic movement, so the letters are jumbled
something embraced is held inside the arms of something else

blocks.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
taken as written
O is a standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A spirited culture is welcomed by a big, long-established nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a southern African kingdom, a nation entirely surrounded by South Africa.

clue.text: Fancy starter of unusual pâté enjoyed with relish?

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are dressed up in a new order
a starter is what comes first, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: first letter of unusual
taken as written, accents dropped

explanation.surface: A posh first course of exotic pâté, eaten with a pickle on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy starter' reads as a smart appetiser and 'relish' as a condiment; in fact relish here means gusto.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat something up is to consume it eagerly, and the phrase also means took great pleasure in, a figurative idiom.

clue.text: Medical specialist demanding every substance around emergency room

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the other words wrap about this piece

blocks.note: every one is all
standard abbreviation for an emergency room
the substance of an argument is its gist

explanation.surface: A doctor who insists that every chemical be kept around the hospital's casualty unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Substance' looks like a chemical, which suits an allergy doctor, but it means the main point of something.
explanation.definitionFit: An allergist is a physician who treats allergies, a type of medical consultant.

clue.text: Night of poetry held in Middle England

indicators.note: held in means contained within, so the letters are sitting inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An evening of verse readings staged in the conservative heartland of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Middle England is the British term for conservative middle-class voters, not an instruction to take middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: E'en is the poetic contraction of even, the old word for evening, so a verse word for night.

clue.text: A big river, mostly deep blue

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
the Nile, Africa's great river

explanation.surface: A large river that is largely dark blue in colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Anil is the indigo plant and the dark blue dye from it, a crossword favourite for that colour.

clue.text: Is part of spreadsheet used to fill in scores and assorted items?

indicators.note: something used to fill in a space goes inside it

blocks.note: scores, many twenties, means a lot
taken as written
a spreadsheet is made up of cells

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a spreadsheet is used for entering marks and a jumble of other data.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scores' looks like test results to be entered in a spreadsheet, but it means a large number.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscellany is a mixed collection of various things, a synonym for assorted items.

clue.text: Top display you might pick up for tech trial

indicators.note: to pick something up is to hear it, so the words are judged by sound

blocks.note: to top is to beat, and to display a quality is to attest it

explanation.surface: A first-rate screen that you might buy to test some technology.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken without a sounded R, beat attest runs together like the two-word answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A beta test is the trial of software by real users before release, a technology trial.

clue.text: Correspondence still centrally stored by company

indicators.note: centrally points to the middle letter of the word before it
something stored by another is kept inside it

blocks.note: a party of people is a company
the middle letter of five-letter still

explanation.surface: Letters that are still kept in the firm's central archive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correspondence' suggests letters on file, but it means matching or equivalence.
explanation.definitionFit: Parity is equality or matching between things, the mathematical sense of correspondence.

clue.text: Non-drinker needing support over summer

blocks.note: a tee is the peg that supports a golf ball
one who sums, someone who totals figures

explanation.surface: A sober person who needs backing throughout the hot months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summer' is the season in the surface but one who does sums in the wordplay; 'over' places the first piece above the second in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotaller abstains completely from alcohol, so is someone who does not drink.

clue.text: Self-contained pit houses with a larder at the front

indicators.note: to house something is to give it a place inside, so these pieces go within
at the front points to the first letter of the word just before

blocks.note: the pit of a fruit is its stone
with means and, joining together
taken as written
first letter of larder

explanation.surface: A self-contained cellar arrangement with a pantry at the front of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pit' reads as a hole in the ground, but here it is the hard seed in a cherry or plum.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-alone thing operates independently, needing nothing else, which is what self-contained describes.

clue.text: Potentially Oscar-winning drama made money outside America finally

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it
a word placed outside another surrounds it

blocks.note: Noh, also spelt No, is classical Japanese drama
to mint coins is literally to make money
last letter of America

explanation.surface: A film tipped for an Academy Award earned a fortune outside the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a box-office hit; NO is the alternative spelling of Japanese Noh theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A film shortlisted for an Academy Award could still win, so being put forward makes it a possible winner.

clue.text: Gentle hint largely designed to impart information

indicators.note: largely means most but not all, so the final letter goes
something designed has been planned and laid out anew, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soft suggestion, mostly intended to pass on knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlighten someone is to give them knowledge or understanding, a synonym for informing them.

clue.text: Plan in principle getting cut down

indicators.note: cut down means shortened, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: ideally, or in an ideal sense, means in principle

explanation.surface: A scheme that is accepted in theory ends up being trimmed back.
explanation.walkthrough: The ideal case is the theoretical one, so 'in principle' stands for that adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea can be a scheme or intention, as in 'the idea is to leave early', a synonym for a plan.

clue.text: Fraud involving computers being recalled

indicators.note: recalling something calls it back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: Macs are Apple computers

explanation.surface: A swindle in which faulty computers are being withdrawn by the manufacturer.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a dishonest scheme to cheat people, a synonym for a fraud.

clue.text: Increase in destruction of a coastline

indicators.note: destruction breaks something apart, so the letters are scattered and rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rise in the erosion of a stretch of shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Escalation is a rapid growth in scale or intensity, so it is a synonym for an increase.

clue.text: Deception hard to prove

blocks.note: a con is a trick or deception
firm means hard or solid

explanation.surface: A trick that is difficult to demonstrate.
explanation.definitionFit: To confirm something is to establish that it is true, a synonym for proving it.

clue.text: Daring performances wow banks of theatregoers

indicators.note: the banks of a river are its two edges, so only the outside letters are kept

blocks.note: to wow an audience is to stun it
first and last letters of theatregoers

explanation.surface: Bold acts that amaze rows of people at a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' suggests tiers of seats in a theatre, but it means the two edges of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stunts are feats of skill and daring done for show, a synonym for bold performances.

clue.text: Fish beneath small rock

indicators.note: beneath places one piece under the next in a down entry, fixing their order

blocks.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
the hake is a sea fish

explanation.surface: A fish lurking under a little stone.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'beneath' puts the fish below the small piece, so it comes second.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock something is to shake it back and forth, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink almost better after the end of Lent

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which is all that is kept

blocks.note: nigh means nearly or almost
last letter of Lent
to cap something is to better or outdo it

explanation.surface: A boozy drink seems the next best thing once the season of Lent is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' tells you the first piece comes after the T; 'better' is a verb meaning outdo, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightcap is a drink, usually alcoholic, taken just before going to bed.

clue.text: Brown bread perfectly absorbs soup at first

indicators.note: something that absorbs takes another thing into itself
at first points to the opening letter of the word before

blocks.note: to a T means perfectly
first letter of soup

explanation.surface: Wholemeal bread is ideal for mopping up soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown bread' looks like the wholemeal loaf; read together it is bread that has been browned. 'To a T' means exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Toast is sliced bread browned by heat, so it is literally bread made brown.

clue.text: Senior cop involved in settlement dispute

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be caught up inside it

blocks.note: a contract is a settled agreement
Detective Inspector, a senior police rank

explanation.surface: A high-ranking police officer gets drawn into a row over an agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settlement dispute' reads as a single phrase, but the last word stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To contradict a statement is to deny or challenge it, a synonym for disputing it.

clue.text: Area covered in fine wood

indicators.note: covered in means wrapped by something else, so this piece goes inside

blocks.note: OK means fine
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A patch coated with a delicate timber veneer.
explanation.definitionFit: Oak is a hard timber from the oak tree, so it is a kind of wood.

clue.text: Colleague is friendly, but not initially

indicators.note: not initially means without the opening letter, so the first letter is removed

blocks.note: pally is informal for friendly

explanation.surface: A workmate is pleasant enough, though not at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is an associate or partner who works alongside you, close in sense to a colleague.

clue.text: Josh, visibly angry about guy stealing new carpet

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards
something stolen is taken in and held, so this letter goes inside

blocks.note: to josh is to tease, or kid
red in the face with anger
a guy is a man, a mister
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Josh, red-faced over a man who made off with a brand-new rug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Josh' looks like a man's name but is the verb meaning tease. Kidderminster is a town in Worcestershire, England, famous for carpet-making.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidderminster carpet is a type of reversible woven carpet named after the town where it was made.
